His one-by-one rulings (#2508, #2038, #2551, #2535, #2026, #2068) all said read it, but each was also a priority call, and the record holds rulings the other way: on 2026-10-23 he ruled that the 'right-angled at X' spellings are not student input and are refused and taught, and his charter rule P10 says non-textbook input is taught, not supported. judgments.question: When some drawing satisfies every given but the tool shows an invalid one (amber, crossed, wrong kind), must it find and draw the valid one?
judgments.ruling: Search first, refuse last: when a free quantity the student left open can make every given hold, the tool searches for that drawing and draws it valid. Every configuration it offers must satisfy the givens, because a drawing that breaks one is not a configuration. It refuses only when nothing the student wrote can save the figure.

precedents.quote: Search first, refuse last. When a letter in the sentence can move the shape, hunt for a value that makes it valid and DRAW it. Refuse only when nothing the student wrote can save it.

judgments.limits: This combines the general search-first rule (given on crossed rings, already applied to #2102, #2443 and #2257) with P13 'not a configuration' and P1. It does not set a bug's priority or how much each class's search may cost. Under docs/17 §7, a correctness feature that doubles replay cost still needs his sign-off. It does not cover what the refusal says when the search fails: that falls under P9 and the 2026-10-15 wording delegation. A shape drawn as a narrower named kind in EVERY configuration is P16's note, not this rule.

judgments.question: When applying a newer ruling changes something he already played and passed, is that a new question or just a Heads-up line?
judgments.reason: No precedent. Nothing in his own words says whether a played-and-passed outcome may be withdrawn on the strength of a newer ruling without asking him. The nearest written rules point toward asking: docs/17 §9 says a plan that reverses an earlier ruling escalates that arm with both rulings quoted, and ADR-W-118's consequences say a session neither preserves the old behaviour nor builds the new one unasked. CLAUDE.md's 'the newer ADR wins' settles which document is authoritative. It does not say whether the reversal needs his confirmation. The question is also about his own approval process: what he must see before a played outcome changes.

judgments.question: When a sentence uses a letter the student has not created yet, does the tool create that point where the sentence puts it?
judgments.ruling: ADR-W-162 is the standing rule: in every builder, a line that refers to a point the figure lacks creates it as a free point (no assumed position, resampled by «הציגו תצורה אחרת») and the line then means what it means when the point exists, so the relation places it; the shared created-points notice names it with a ✕ that removes the line; no 'declare the point first' refusal is taught for a missing point (option A's creation half, without its teach-«נקודה X»-first refusal, plus the notice).

judgments.question: When a sentence says «המעגל», «the circle», «הוא/היא» or a role word, which object does it mean?
judgments.reason: No precedent for the pronoun half. Card e22 (2026-10-24) rules the definite «המעגל» only, in three circle forms: one drawn circle → bind it; two → ask which; none → a new circle. ADR-685 rules the definite triangle noun with two candidates as a refusal that names both, which is not the same as the ask. The «הוא עובר דרך …» question on #2619 (a line and a circle are both masculine) was put to him and never answered; it was orphaned when ADR-W-167 superseded that plan. judgments.question: Which stated values appear on the figure, and what happens to a stated value with no natural place to draw it (a perimeter, a circumference, a radius)?
judgments.ruling: A stated perimeter (of any shape, including a circle's circumference and an arc's length) and a stated radius are never drawn on the figure, in any tool. They stay givens and are shown off the figure. Nothing new is drawn just to carry such a value's label. Every other stated value stays on the figure (B2).

His words keep a perimeter off the diagram and in the givens; they do not say whether it is also printed in the data panel. A stated area keeps its label (#2244: a circle area is drawn on the circle).

judgments.question: How thin or squashed may a drawing be when the student gave no number that forces it?

judgments.question: May the tool's ANSWER use a curve form the student is not allowed to TYPE (a shifted parabola, a rotated conic)?

Naming a shifted parabola as a locus answer widens that promise and the scope of the locus feature. None of his rulings found covers answers outside the canonical family; his conic rulings (2026-10-30, "now we need to build all capabilities") are about the canonical ellipse and parabola.

judgments.question: When a student adds a line, may points they placed earlier move at all, and by how much?
judgments.reason: No precedent decides whether small movement of untouched earlier objects is acceptable, or the exact/minimal/by-value split the options offer. His rulings say a given resizes a drawn figure in place instead of redrawing it (#2039) and that a later circle must not re-bind an earlier letter so AB stays put (#2333), and CLAUDE.md says a constraint never makes the figure jump; none of these sets a tolerance or says which objects may move. The question itself records that no ruling covers it.

judgments.question: When a number is written in a form that could mean two things («2 3», «2 1/2»), is it refused with a teaching sentence before the AI, in every builder?
judgments.ruling: Two numbers with only a space between them («2 3»), and a number then a space then a fraction («2 1/2»), are refused with a teaching sentence before the AI in every builder. They are never multiplied and never sent to the model.

precedents.quote: Follow analytic. «2 1/2» is refused with the teaching sentence (2.5, 2+1/2, 2*1/2), and «2½» reads 2.5. Any 'number space number' is refused, so «|z| = 2 3» no longer reads 6.
2-D and 3-D refuse «2 1/2» before the AI, with analytic's teaching sentence.

judgments.limits: A general rule built from consistent one-off rulings: analytic «5 1/2» (#2222), 2-D and 3-D «2 1/2» (#2248), and complex's "Any 'number space number' is refused" (ADR-CX-081). It also follows from the honesty invariant (a stated value is never silently changed) and from B1 (one verdict for one sentence). He has not ruled «2 3» directly for 2-D, 3-D or analytic. Not decided: the exact teaching sentence for the «2 3» form in those builders, which goes to him under ADR-W-122, and any priority.

judgments.question: How is a helper line the student did not draw as a segment shown — dashed or solid?
judgments.reason: His ruling covers only extensions: a construction point off the ink gets its carrying line extended, dashed (ADR-W-124, 2-D and analytic; 3-D on flat figures, #1984). On #1984 he explicitly kept for himself the case of an extension that could pass behind a solid's face. Nothing he said sets the style of a directrix or of other helper lines, and «מקווקו» on a circle (#2336) is a style the student chooses, not a helper rule. Option A's 'every extension, directrix or helper' goes past his words.

option A — the same dashed extension as 2-D (ADR-W-124), on flat figures. When an extension could pass behind a solid's face, the question comes back to him.
